messages:
sahil: Heads-up — ran a combined nsys + perfetto pass on a repro box. Observed a repeating HBM bandwidth 'waveform' spike that lines up exactly with KV-cache eviction bursts when seq_len > 4096. Attached perfetto timeline (s3).

alex: link? also which model + kernel selection policy was active for the run?

perf-bot: Trace uploaded: https://s3.company.internal/traces/2543216789/perfetto.pbz (nsys files in same folder) :white_check_mark:

sahil: @alex model=redwood-open-7B, quantized path=8-bit, kernel_policy=dynamic-latency (default). Repro steps in the trace: 50 concurrent requests, microbatch=1, avg_seq=512 but tails to 8192 for ~2% of requests.

irene: quick glances at the perfetto timeline: the HBM BW spike is ~3s after a large KV reclaim sweep. Kernel timeline shows a burst of small attention kernels + memcpy kernels queued right after eviction. Looks like eviction triggers DMA storms and kernel scheduling jitter.

maria: can you paste the nsys kernel timeline snippet? curious whether kernels are being dispatched back-to-back or if there's a gap where DMA saturates.

sahil: paste from nsys (condensed):

```
Time(ms)   GPU Op                 Duration(ms)   Notes
12013.2     memcpyHtoD               0.48
12013.8     aten::attention_fwd      0.82
12014.7     memcpyDtoH               0.44
12015.1     kv_cache_evict           2.25   <-- large
12017.4     memcpyHtoD               1.10
12018.6     aten::attention_fwd      0.90
12019.6     kernel_dispatch_idle     0.30
12019.9     memcpyDtoH               1.35
```

sahil: note the big kv_cache_evict kernel and subsequent memcpy bursts. Bandwidth graphs show sustained HBM saturations ~500GB/s during eviction window.

alex: that eviction blocking kernel could be holding locks that force the runtime to push many small attention kernels (micro ops) causing lots of small memcpys. Two hypotheses: (1) eviction is synchronous and stalls host threads causing serialized DMA; (2) kernel selection chooses high-throughput kernels that are sensitive to memory contention for long tails.

sam: repro command I used to capture nvprof/ncu:

```
# run on repro node
LD_PRELOAD=/opt/prof/nvtx/libnvtx.so nsys profile --output out.nsys --trace=cuda,osrt ./serve_local --model redwood-open-7B --concurrency 50 --tail-rate 0.02 --max-seq 8192
ncu --set full --target-processes all --export out.ncu out.nsys
```

sam: ncu suggests the memcpy kernels are using pageable-to-device paths sometimes (unexpected), which explodes HBM traffic due to pinned memory fallback. Also saw increased L2 cache miss rates on the attention kernels during the eviction window.

irene: Interesting. If the KV eviction path is doing a full-page walk and falling back to pageable copies, that could explain DMA thrash. Two quick experiments to try: (A) make eviction async (avoid stall on host threads) and (B) change kernel selection to prefer kernels with lower memory footprint (even if slightly higher compute) for seq_len>2048.

maria: +1 for experiments. For (B) can we add a temporary override in runtime config? e.g.

```
# runtime override
kernel_selection_override:
  seq_len_threshold: 2048
  prefer_low_mem_kernels: true
```

alex: I can land a quick flag to force non-prefetching eviction to be async and queue KV-cleanup on a background worker. Will run the same trace after.

sahil: timeline after alex's async-evict patch (short run): HBM spikes reduced by ~65%, memcpy tail durations shorter, and attention kernels show ~30% fewer L2 misses. Re-running with kernel_selection_override produced another ~20% drop in tail latency for those heavy seq requests.

irene: great. Next steps: (1) alex to open PR for async eviction + test harness (perf regression tests), (2) sam to add an ncu check for pageable-copy detection during CI traces, (3) ops to schedule a longer soak with mixed tails to validate throughput impact.

alex: filing PR and perf job now. PR will include a small perf test and a perf-bot annotation so traces auto-upload.

perf-bot: Created perf job: job/2543216789-async-evict-smoke, artifacts will be at s3://traces/2543216789/job-id.

maria: thanks all — great find. tagging this for postmortem note for runtime heuristics and adding an item to the batcher heuristics doc to account for pageable-copy fallbacks. :memo:
